why: Inserting the core principle to avoid cuts immediately after finite auxiliaries/coproducts caused the bander to re-rank many early cut positions: it suppressed some late/secondary cuts but also shifted several top-ranked cuts earlier (splitting subjects vs auxiliaries and fragmenting enumerations). That produced balanced numbers of better/worse pairs and a small net mean change, while degrading rank coincidence at depths 1–4 (so long-latency behaviour worsened even as a few short-bin scores improved).
lesson: A revision that penalizes cuts after auxiliaries/copoläs must not change the top-1..4 ranked choices or induce earlier subject/auxiliary or enumeration splits — constrain the change so shallow (long-latency) ranks remain stable and check per-bin effects before adopting.
